sections.name: i_tonic_plane
sections.notes: I opens and closes the cycle but only holds 16 of 64 bars total (25%, down from the original's 50/50 I/IV split). ii and bVII give real color without leaving the D pedal, since bass_style=pedal locks to the FIRST chord's root (I=D) for the whole section.

sections.name: ii_subdominant_tide
sections.notes: No I chord at all in this section. Progression starts on IV, so pedal (style_pedal locks to chords[0]'s root) shifts to G for the whole section -- a real key-center drift, not just a different chord above the same bass. bVI (Bb) and bVII (C) pull toward Mixolydian/Aeolian color; the ear loses the D anchor entirely for roughly 3.5 minutes.

sections.name: iii_dominant_haze
sections.notes: Pedal moves again, this time to A (v = A minor is chords[0], so bass locks to A). Using the minor dominant rather than major V keeps this non-functional/non-cadential -- no leading tone pulling back to D, just another plane to sit on. No I chord anywhere in this section.

sections.name: iv_return_recolored
sections.notes: D pedal returns (chords[0]=I) for a sense of homecoming after two sections away, but I itself only holds 14 of 64 bars (22%) -- vi, bVII and bVI do most of the work. This mirrors the original's ABA instinct without the original's I/IV 50-50 monotony.
